title: An outside birth takes a marked clock ancestor’s last loose distinction
standard_statement: In a serial incidence process with eligibility recomputed after each birth, do two continuations of an identical reachable state differ because an outside event exhausts a necessary parent’s final slot? Require full ground-truth histories and uniqueness against future substitutes.
nearest_known: The preceding clock comparison changed original supplies, or triggered a prior-common-child veto while funds remained. Neither exhibits a matched physical last-slot loss.
claim: Two raw histories from identical holdings diverge at birth 10 when an outside birth exhausts an indispensable original donor. The unchanged clock completes at birth 21, and the other arm can never complete the same turn. Removing one common expense lets the very same outside spend coexist with the turn. A boundary theorem covers all prefixes of distinct required roles before the first outside spend on this source.
prospective_advisor: Independent GPT-6.2 Astra at maximum reasoning reviewed both design versions and cleared the exact revised digest before freezing.
epistemic_class: Constructive finite permanent-loss witness and an all-orders exclusion theorem for a named class of prefixes.
source_contribution: Identifies equal-source and equal-prefix causal competition for the very same physical distinction, and independently reconstructs the clock's required ancestry and surviving counterfactual.
scope: First marked 20-role turn of the paid eight-original clock with one marked spare at 0, the extra source holder at 3 and one raw birth at a time. Clock ancestry is read from the supplied originals and successive physical writes.
nonclaims: No claim about how often either outcome occurs across admissible histories.
Strict joins-first from the original source is outside the exhibited histories.
The outside parent is the attached original. The exhausted donor is an original needed by a clock ancestor.
Arbitrary continuations after the disjoint expense on originals 2 and 8 remain unresolved.
The sufficient-cause argument allows other structural changes at the same birth.

validation.status: Passed written proof, per-input law and history checks, independent in-task reconstruction and direct relation checks for arity 3 through 8.
